items.title: No interest on over-limit loan EMIs from May 2026
items.summary: If you carry a balance on your Axis card, interest is charged on your unpaid dues and on billed EMIs — but from 30 May 2026, EMIs for the Over-the-Limit Instant Loan are carved out and won't attract that interest. That's a small saving for anyone revolving a balance while repaying an OTL loan.

items.title: Horizon card fee waived for new Burgundy savers
items.summary: The ₹3,000 joining and annual fee on the Axis Bank Horizon Credit Card becomes nil if you hold a Burgundy Savings Account opened on or after 1 July 2026. Axis says this waiver is at its discretion and can be pulled back anytime.

items.title: Magnus card free for new Burgundy Salary customers
items.summary: The ₹12,500 joining and annual fee on the Magnus Credit Card is dropped to nil if you have a Burgundy Salary Account opened on or after 1 July 2026. Everyone else keeps paying ₹12,500 plus GST unless they hit the spend waiver.

items.title: Final billed amount can differ from what you approved
items.summary: On fuel, international spends, rent, wallet loads and some merchant payments, the amount finally charged to your card may be higher than the amount you approved, because taxes, surcharges and exchange rates get added at settlement. Check your statement rather than the payment screen for the real cost.

items.title: Cardless cash withdrawal ends 21 Feb 2026
items.summary: You will no longer be able to pull cash from RBL or non-RBL ATMs without your card once this service stops on 21 February 2026. Until then it still costs Rs. 20 per transaction, and that fee is not refunded if the transaction expires or is cancelled.

items.title: Rent and wallet spends don't earn you a fee waiver
items.summary: Rent, wallet, utility, government, EMI and cash transactions no longer count towards the spending target that gets your annual fee refunded. You need that much more genuine shopping to get the waiver.

items.title: Insurance, gold, fuel no longer count for fee waiver
items.summary: Spends on insurance, gold and fuel stopped counting towards the annual fee waiver target on these premium cards, so hitting the waiver is harder. Rent, wallet, utility, government, EMI and cash spends were already excluded.

items.title: 1% fee on fuel spends over Rs 50,000 a month
items.summary: If your petrol and diesel spends cross Rs 50,000 in a statement cycle, Axis charges 1% plus GST on them. Below that, no fee applies.

items.title: 1% fee on gaming spends over Rs 10,000 a month
items.summary: Spending Rs 10,000 or more on online skill-based gaming platforms in one statement cycle now costs 1% plus GST. Below that threshold nothing is charged.

items.title: 1% fee on school fees paid via apps
items.summary: Paying tuition or school fees through third-party apps now costs 1% plus GST on every transaction. Paying the institution directly on its own website or card machine stays free.

items.title: 1% fee on utility bills over Rs 25,000 a month
items.summary: Electricity, water and similar bills totalling Rs 25,000 or more in a statement cycle now attract a 1% plus GST charge. Under Rs 25,000 in a cycle, there is no fee.

items.title: 1% fee on wallet loads over Rs 10,000 a month
items.summary: Loading Paytm-type wallets with Rs 10,000 or more in one statement cycle now costs you 1% plus GST on those loads. Stay under Rs 10,000 in a cycle and nothing is charged.

items.title: No interest on over-limit loan EMIs from May 2026
items.summary: If you are revolving a balance, EMIs for an Over-the-Limit Instant Loan will stop attracting interest from 30 May 2026. All other billed EMIs still get charged interest.

items.title: Horizon card free for new Burgundy savings accounts
items.summary: The Rs 3,000 joining and annual fee on the Horizon card is waived if your Burgundy Savings Account is opened on or after 1 July 2026. The waiver is at the bank's discretion and needs the Burgundy relationship maintained.

items.title: Magnus fee free for new Burgundy salary accounts
items.summary: You save the Rs 12,500 joining and annual fee on Magnus if your Burgundy Salary Account is opened on or after 1 July 2026. Axis can withdraw this at any time and you must keep the Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Extra Rs 100 if you miss minimum due twice
items.summary: Missing your minimum amount due for two cycles in a row adds Rs 100 on top of the normal late fee, and it repeats every cycle until you clear it. Paying at least the minimum stops it.

items.title: Refunds on foreign spends cost you 3.5%
items.summary: When you return something you bought abroad, Axis keeps an extra 3.5% of the refunded amount. So a cancelled foreign purchase leaves you out of pocket.

items.title: IndiGo card perks fully switched off
items.summary: All features and benefits on the 6E Rewards IndiGo cards ended on 1 December 2025, and any 6E Rewards you had were converted to IndiGo BluChips on 1 November 2025. Existing holders have been moved to a different HDFC card.

items.title: Infinia now needs ₹18L spends a year to keep
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you must spend ₹18 lakh a year on your Infinia card, or keep ₹50 lakh in average balances with HDFC, to stay on the Infinia programme. Fall short and the bank can move you off the card and its benefits.

items.title: New 1.75% markup on rupee spends abroad
items.summary: If you pay in rupees at an overseas shop, website or an India-based merchant registered abroad, HDFC will now add a 1.75% markup on top of the bill. This applies to all such transactions from 15 May 2026.

items.title: Late fee up to ₹1,300 if you miss a Jumbo Loan EMI
items.summary: Missing or part-paying an Insta Jumbo Loan EMI now attracts a slab-based late fee plus GST, from ₹100 on small dues to ₹1,300 when you owe more than ₹50,000. It kicks in from 20 June 2026.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad gets costlier from 15 Jan 2026
items.summary: ICICI is revising the Dynamic Currency Conversion fee charged when you pay in Indian rupees at an overseas shop or to a foreign-registered merchant in India. Most cards will be charged 3.50% of the transaction, while Times Black pays 1.49%, Emeralde cards 2.00%, MakeMyTrip Travel 0.99% and Amazon Pay 1.99%.

items.title: BookMyShow perks need ₹25,000 spend each quarter
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you only get BookMyShow benefits if you spent at least ₹25,000 on your ICICI card in the previous quarter, so light users lose the perk. For example, spending ₹25,000 between 26 December 2025 and 25 March 2026 unlocks the benefit for April–June 2026.

items.title: Cardless ATM cash withdrawal ends Feb 21, 2026
items.summary: RBL is shutting down IMT cardless cash withdrawals at RBL and non-RBL ATMs from 21 February 2026, so you'll need your debit card to take out cash. Until then the service still costs Rs. 20 per transaction, and that fee is not refunded if the transaction expires or is cancelled.

items.title: CASHBACK SBI Card benefits are being changed
items.summary: The benefits on your CASHBACK SBI Credit Card are being revised from 1 April 2026, so check what you'll actually earn before your next big spend. The notice links to the details rather than listing old and new values.

items.title: Only 60,000 points a month for statement credit
items.summary: You can no longer wipe out a big bill with points in one go — statement credit redemption is capped at 60,000 points per month. Air India SBI Signature and the two PhonePe cards are exempt from this cap.

items.title: Statement credit only in blocks of 4,000 points
items.summary: You must redeem points for statement credit in multiples of 4,000, so leftover points below that stay stuck in your account. PhonePe SBI Card PURPLE and SELECT BLACK are excluded from this rule.

items.title: BPCL card: spend Rs.1 lakh to skip the Rs.499 fee
items.summary: You now have to spend twice as much in a year to get the Rs.499 annual fee waived on the BPCL SBI Credit Card — Rs.1 lakh instead of Rs.50,000. Spend less than that and the fee stays on your bill.

items.title: Small unpaid bills now attract a late fee
items.summary: Missing payment on a small balance now costs you: dues over Rs.100 attract a Rs.100 late fee (earlier nothing was charged below Rs.500), and dues in the Rs.500–1,000 band jump from Rs.400 to Rs.500. Larger slabs stay the same.

items.title: PhonePe Purple card: monthly reward cap cut
items.summary: You'll earn fewer points each month on your PhonePe SBI Card PURPLE — the monthly cap on PhonePe spends drops from 1,000 points to 750 (just 250 for insurance), and online spends drop from 1,000 to 750 points. That's roughly a quarter to three-quarters less reward value per month.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black: more spends earn zero points
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 tolls, gifts, jewellery, education fees, and utility, insurance or UPI payments made outside the PhonePe app earn no reward points at all. Route these through the PhonePe app if you want points.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black: reward cap halved online
items.summary: Your monthly reward ceiling on the PhonePe SBI Card SELECT BLACK falls sharply — online spends go from 2,000 points to 1,000, and PhonePe spends from 2,000 to 1,500 (only 500 for insurance). Big spenders lose up to half their monthly points.

items.title: Overlimit spends will cost INR 550 each time
items.summary: YES BANK is bringing back the overlimit facility, so a transaction that goes past your credit limit can go through — but it will cost you INR 550 plus GST each time. Watch your limit if you don't want the charge.

items.title: POP-Club fuel waiver limited to INR 100 a month
items.summary: On the POP-Club card, the 1% fuel surcharge waiver now only applies to fill-ups between INR 1,000 and INR 3,500, and you can get back a maximum of INR 100 per statement cycle. Anything outside that band gets no waiver.

items.title: ATM cash withdrawal fee jumps to min INR 650
items.summary: Taking cash out on your YES BANK credit card will cost you at least INR 650 instead of INR 500 from 15 June 2026. The 2.5% rate stays the same, so small withdrawals get much pricier.

items.title: Failed auto-debit now costs up to INR 5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces, the fee rises from 2% (min INR 450) to 2.5% (min INR 500), and the monthly cap jumps from INR 1,500 to INR 5,000 per statement. Keep enough balance in your account on the due date.

items.title: Foreign spends get costlier on most cards
items.summary: The forex mark-up on overseas and international online spends rises on several cards from 15 June 2026 — for example Select and Ace go from 2.75% to 3.50%, Reserv and YES First Preferred from 1.75% to 2.00%, and Elite+ from 2.75% to 3.00%. YES Private (0.50%), Marquee (1.00%) and FREO (3.40%) stay unchanged.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver band changes on most cards
items.summary: The transaction range that qualifies for the 1% fuel surcharge waiver is being redrawn per card — for most cards the old INR 400–5,000 band becomes INR 500–3,000, while Paisabazaar Paisasave moves from INR 500–3,000 to INR 500–3,000 and premium cards get INR 500–5,000. Small fills below INR 500 will no longer get the waiver on cards that earlier started at INR 400.

items.title: New INR 250 fee for paying by cheque at branch
items.summary: Dropping a cheque at a YES BANK branch to pay a card bill of INR 1,000 or more will now cost INR 250 plus GST. This charge did not exist before.

items.title: Paying your card bill in cash now costs ₹500
items.summary: Depositing cash at a YES Bank branch to pay your card bill will cost ₹500 plus GST instead of ₹100, for any payment of ₹1,000 or more. Pay online instead and you avoid it entirely.

items.title: Replacing a lost card now costs Rs 199, not Rs 100
items.summary: Getting a new plastic card after loss, theft or damage will cost INR 199 per replacement from 15 June 2026, up from INR 100. Fees for BYOC eco-friendly and metal cards stay the same.

items.title: Insurance, gold and fuel no longer count for fee waiver
items.summary: Spending on insurance, gold and fuel will no longer count towards the annual spend target that gets your annual fee waived, so hitting the waiver is harder. Rent, wallet, utilities, government, EMIs and cash withdrawals were already excluded.

items.title: Interest on unpaid dues is 3.75% a month
items.summary: If you carry a balance, most Axis cards charge 3.75% per month, which works out to 55.55% a year, plus GST. Reserve and Magnus are lower at 3.0% a month and Burgundy Private at 1.5%.

items.title: New 1% fee on fuel spends above ₹50,000
items.summary: Fuel purchases add up to more than ₹50,000 in a statement cycle and you pay 1% plus tax on the total — ₹500 on ₹50,000. Below that, nothing is charged.

items.title: New 1% fee on gaming spends above ₹10,000
items.summary: Spend over ₹10,000 in a statement cycle on online skill-based gaming platforms and you pay 1% plus tax on the total. Under ₹10,000 in the cycle, no fee applies.

items.title: New 1% fee on school and college fees via apps
items.summary: Paying education fees through a third-party app now costs 1% plus tax on every transaction — ₹100 on ₹10,000. Paying the institution directly on its own website or card machine is still free.

items.title: New 1% fee on utility bills above ₹25,000
items.summary: Electricity, water and similar bills totalling over ₹25,000 in a statement cycle now attract 1% plus tax — ₹250 on ₹25,000. Paying under ₹25,000 in the cycle avoids the fee.

items.title: New 1% fee on wallet top-ups above ₹10,000
items.summary: Load more than ₹10,000 into Paytm-type wallets in one statement cycle and you pay 1% plus tax on it — ₹120 on ₹12,000. Stay under ₹10,000 in the cycle and there is no fee.

items.title: Paying rent by card: ₹1,500 fee cap is gone
items.summary: You still pay a 1% fee plus tax on every rent payment made with an Axis credit card, but the old ₹1,500 per-transaction ceiling no longer appears — a ₹3 lakh rent payment now costs ₹3,000 plus GST instead of ₹1,500. Olympus and Primus cards pay nothing on rent.

items.title: Horizon card free for new Burgundy Savings customers
items.summary: The ₹3,000 joining and annual fee on the Horizon card is nil if you hold a Burgundy Savings Account opened on or after 1 July 2026. Axis can revise or withdraw this offer at any time.

items.title: Magnus fee waived for new Burgundy Salary customers
items.summary: You save the ₹12,500 joining and annual fee on the Magnus card if you have a Burgundy Salary Account opened on or after 1 July 2026. The bank can withdraw this at any time and you must keep the Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Extra ₹100 if you miss the minimum twice in a row
items.summary: Miss your Minimum Amount Due for two consecutive statement cycles and an extra ₹100 is added on top of the normal late payment fee. It keeps repeating every cycle until you clear the minimum.

items.title: Refunds on foreign spends cost you an extra 3.5%
items.summary: When you get a refund on an international transaction, Axis charges an additional 3.5% fee on it, on top of the 3.5% forex markup you already paid on the purchase. So a cancelled overseas order leaves you out of pocket.

items.title: Times Titanium forex fee jumps from 2% to 3.5%
items.summary: Spending abroad on the Times Titanium card now costs 3.5% of the transaction as a foreign currency markup instead of 2%. That is an extra ₹150 on every ₹10,000 you spend overseas.

items.title: IndiGo 6E card perks are gone for good
items.summary: All features and benefits on the 6E Rewards and 6E Rewards XL cards stopped on 1 December 2025, and the cards are no longer issued. Any 6E Rewards you had were auto-converted to IndiGo BluChips on 1 November 2025 instead of moving to your new card.

items.title: Keep Infinia only if you spend ₹18L a year
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you must spend ₹18 lakh a year on the card (primary plus add-ons) or hold ₹50 lakh in average balances with HDFC to keep your Infinia. Fall short and the bank can move you off the programme.

items.title: New 1.75% markup on rupee-billed foreign payments
items.summary: From 15 May 2026 you'll pay an extra 1.75% whenever you swipe abroad in rupees or pay an India-based merchant that's registered overseas. On a ₹50,000 booking that's ₹875 extra.

items.title: Late fee now applies on missed Insta Jumbo loan EMIs
items.summary: From 20 June 2026, missing or part-paying an Insta Jumbo loan EMI adds a late fee plus GST, ranging from ₹100 to ₹1,300 depending on how much you owe. Nothing is charged if the outstanding is ₹100 or less.

items.title: New fee when you pay in rupees abroad
items.summary: From 15 January 2026 ICICI charges a Dynamic Currency Conversion fee every time you pay in Indian rupees at an overseas merchant or an India-based merchant registered abroad — 3.50% on most cards, 2.00% on Emeralde cards, 1.99% on Amazon Pay, 1.49% on Times Black and 0.99% on the MakeMyTrip Travel card. Always choose to pay in the local currency to dodge this.

items.title: BookMyShow perk now needs ₹25,000 spends a quarter
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you only get the BookMyShow movie benefit if you spent at least ₹25,000 on your card in the previous quarter, so light spenders lose it. Spends between 26 December 2025 and 25 March 2026 decide your April–June 2026 benefit.

items.title: Points on discount offers taken back within 120 days
items.summary: For offers launched from 15 January 2026, points earned on cashback offers will be clawed back within 90 days of the cashback posting, and on instant discount offers within 120 days of the offer month ending. Don't count those points as yours until that window passes.

items.title: CASHBACK SBI Card benefits are being changed
items.summary: SBI Card says the benefits on the CASHBACK SBI Credit Card change from 1 April 2026, with details in a linked document. Check what your cashback looks like before you plan big spends.

items.title: Statement credit only in blocks of 4,000 points
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can redeem points for statement credit only in multiples of 4,000, so leftover points below that stay stuck until you build up more. PhonePe PURPLE and SELECT BLACK cards are excluded from this rule.

items.title: Statement credit redemption capped at 60,000 points
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can convert only 60,000 reward points to statement credit in a month, so large point balances take longer to cash out. Air India SBI Signature and both PhonePe cards are exempt from this cap.

items.title: BPCL card: spend 2x more to get the fee waived
items.summary: From 1 May 2026 you must spend Rs.1 Lakh a year instead of Rs.50,000 to get the Rs.499 annual fee refunded on the BPCL SBI Card. Spend less and you simply pay the fee.

items.title: New Rs.100 late fee on small unpaid bills from May
items.summary: From 1 May 2026 you'll pay a Rs.100 late fee if you miss paying an outstanding of just Rs.101–500, which was free earlier, and the Rs.501–1,000 slab jumps from Rs.400 to Rs.500. Bigger slabs stay the same.

items.title: No PhonePe card points on tolls, fees, jewellery, UPI
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 both PhonePe SBI cards stop earning any reward points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, school and college fees, and on utilities, insurance or UPI paid outside the PhonePe app. Pay these elsewhere if you want points.

items.title: PhonePe PURPLE monthly reward caps cut sharply
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your monthly reward ceiling on PhonePe spends drops from 1,000 points to 750 points (only 250 of which can come from insurance), and online spends drop from 1,000 to 750 points. That's roughly a quarter less rewards each month if you were maxing out.

items.title: PhonePe SELECT BLACK reward caps halved online
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 the monthly cap on online spends falls from 2,000 to 1,000 points, and PhonePe spends fall from 2,000 to 1,500 points with only 500 allowed from insurance. Heavy users will earn noticeably less each month.

items.title: ₹550 charge returns if you cross your credit limit
items.summary: YES Bank is bringing back the overlimit facility, and every transaction that pushes you past your credit limit will cost a flat ₹550 plus GST. Your card will still work above the limit, but you pay for it.

items.title: POP-CLUB fuel waiver only on ₹1,000–₹3,500 fills
items.summary: On the POP-CLUB card the 1% fuel surcharge waiver applies only to fuel spends between ₹1,000 and ₹3,500, with a maximum of ₹100 back per statement cycle. Fill-ups outside that range get no waiver.

items.title: Cash withdrawal fee jumps from ₹500 to ₹650
items.summary: Taking cash out on your YES Bank credit card will cost 2.5% or ₹650, whichever is higher, instead of the earlier ₹650 floor of ₹500. That's ₹150 more on every small ATM cash advance from 15 June 2026.

items.title: Failed auto-debit now costs more, cap raised to ₹5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces, the penalty rises from 2% or ₹450 to 2.5% or ₹500 (whichever is higher), and the monthly ceiling jumps from ₹1,500 to ₹5,000. Repeated bounces in one statement can now cost you over three times as much.

items.title: Forex markup on Select and ACE cards goes 2.75% to 3.5%
items.summary: International spends on these cards will cost 3.5% in markup instead of 2.75%. That's ₹375 extra on a ₹50,000 overseas transaction.

items.title: Forex markup rises to 2% on Reserv and YES First cards
items.summary: Spending abroad or on foreign websites gets costlier: the markup goes from 1.75% to 2% of the transaction. On a ₹50,000 foreign spend that's ₹125 extra.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver now starts at ₹500, caps vary
items.summary: The petrol fill-up amounts that qualify for the 1% surcharge waiver are being reset by card: ₹500–₹5,000 on premium cards, ₹500–₹4,000 on Elite+/Reserv/Essence, and ₹500–₹3,000 on ACE, Select, Wellness and similar cards. Small fills below ₹500 no longer get the waiver on most cards.

items.title: Lost card replacement fee doubles to ₹199
items.summary: Getting a replacement for a lost, stolen or damaged plastic card will cost ₹199 instead of ₹100. Eco-friendly and metal BYOC cards keep their existing fees.

items.title: 1% fee on fuel spends above ₹50,000 a month
items.summary: If your fuel spends cross ₹50,000 in one statement cycle, a 1% fee plus tax is charged on that amount — roughly ₹500 on ₹50,000. Below that, no fee.

items.title: 1% fee on gaming spends above ₹10,000 a month
items.summary: Spending ₹10,000 or more on online skill-based gaming platforms in a statement cycle now costs 1% plus tax on that amount. Under ₹10,000 in a cycle, nothing is charged.

items.title: 1% fee on school or college fees paid via apps
items.summary: Paying education fees through third-party apps now costs 1% plus tax on every transaction, so ₹1 lakh of fees costs an extra ₹1,000. Paying the institution directly on its own website or card machine is still free.

items.title: 1% fee on utility bills above ₹25,000 a month
items.summary: Electricity, gas and similar bill payments crossing ₹25,000 in one statement cycle now attract a 1% fee plus tax. Keep the total under ₹25,000 in a cycle to avoid it.

items.title: 1% fee on wallet loads above ₹10,000 a month
items.summary: Loading ₹10,000 or more into Paytm-type wallets in one statement cycle now attracts a 1% fee plus tax on the whole amount. Stay under ₹10,000 in a cycle and nothing is charged.

items.title: Horizon fee waived for new Burgundy savings accounts
items.summary: The ₹3,000 joining and annual fee on the Horizon card becomes nil if you hold a Burgundy Savings Account opened on or after 1 July 2026. Axis can withdraw this at its discretion and you must keep the Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Magnus fee waived for new Burgundy salary accounts
items.summary: The ₹12,500 joining and annual fee on the Magnus card drops to zero if you have a Burgundy Salary Account opened on or after 1 July 2026. The waiver lasts only while you keep that Burgundy relationship.

items.title: ₹1,500 cap on rent fee is gone
items.summary: The 1% rent payment fee no longer stops at ₹1,500 per transaction, so a ₹5 lakh rent payment now costs ₹5,000 plus GST instead of ₹1,500. Only Olympus and Primus cards are exempt.

items.title: Extra ₹100 if you miss minimum due twice in a row
items.summary: Miss the minimum amount due two statement cycles running and Axis adds ₹100 on top of the normal late fee, and keeps charging it every cycle until you clear the minimum. This is over and above the existing late payment fee.

items.title: Paying abroad in rupees now costs 1.5%, not 1%
items.summary: If you let an overseas machine or website bill you in Indian rupees, Axis now charges 1.5% plus tax on that amount instead of 1%. Burgundy Private, Olympus and Primus cardholders pay nothing.

items.title: New 1.75% fee when you pay in rupees abroad
items.summary: From 15 May 2026, paying in Indian rupees at an overseas terminal (or at an India-based merchant registered abroad) will cost you an extra 1.75% markup on the bill. Always choose to pay in the local currency to dodge this charge.

items.title: Late fees now apply on Insta Jumbo loan EMIs too
items.summary: From 20 June 2026, missing or part-paying an Insta Jumbo loan EMI adds a late fee plus GST, starting at ₹100 for dues of ₹101-₹500 and rising to ₹1,300 when you owe more than ₹50,000. Dues of ₹100 or less attract nothing.

items.title: Govt payments now count as utility spends
items.summary: Government transactions are now treated as utility payments, so they follow your card's utility reward rules and caps instead of normal spends. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad gets pricier from Jan 15
items.summary: From 15 January 2026, ICICI revises the Dynamic Currency Conversion fee charged when you pay in Indian rupees at an overseas merchant or at an India-based merchant registered abroad. Most cards will be charged 3.50% of the transaction, while Amazon Pay is 1.99%, Emeralde cards 2.00%, Times Black 1.49% and MakeMyTrip Travel 0.99%.

items.title: Free BookMyShow perks need ₹25,000 spend first
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you only get BookMyShow benefits on eligible ICICI cards if you spent at least ₹25,000 in the previous spend quarter. Spend less and you lose the movie benefit for the next three months.

items.title: Cap of 60,000 points a month for statement credit
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can convert only 60,000 reward points per month into statement credit, so large point balances take longer to cash out. Air India SBI Signature and both PhonePe SBI cards are exempt.

items.title: CASHBACK SBI Card benefits are changing in April
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 the benefits on the CASHBACK SBI Credit Card are being revised, so check the linked details before relying on your current cashback. The notice does not print the old and new values on this page.

items.title: Statement credit redemption only in 4,000-point blocks
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can redeem points for statement credit only in multiples of 4,000, so leftover points below that stay stuck until you build them up. Both PhonePe SBI cards are exempt.

items.title: BPCL card: spend 2x more to skip the Rs.499 fee
items.summary: From 1 May 2026 you must spend Rs.1 lakh in a year to get the Rs.499 annual fee refunded, double the earlier Rs.50,000. Spend less and you simply pay the fee.

items.title: Late payment fee now starts at just Rs.100 overdue
items.summary: From 1 May 2026 you'll be charged Rs.100 if you leave more than Rs.100 unpaid (earlier anything under Rs.500 was free), and the Rs.500-Rs.1,000 slab jumps from Rs.400 to Rs.500. Bigger overdue slabs stay the same.

items.title: PhonePe PURPLE monthly reward caps cut
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your monthly reward points on PhonePe spends drop from 1,000 to 750 (and only 250 for insurance), and online spends drop from 1,000 to 750. That's fewer points every month for the same spending.

items.title: PhonePe Purple: no points on tolls, jewellery, fees
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 you stop earning any reward points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, school/college fees, and on utility, insurance or UPI payments made outside the PhonePe app. Spending in these categories now earns you nothing.

items.title: PhonePe SELECT BLACK reward caps halved online
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 monthly points on online spends fall from 2,000 to 1,000, and PhonePe spends fall from 2,000 to 1,500 (only 500 for insurance). New exclusions also mean no points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, college fees, and utilities, insurance or UPI outside the PhonePe app.

items.title: New Rs 550 charge for spending over your limit
items.summary: From 1 June 2026 YES BANK lets some transactions go through above your credit limit, and charges INR 550 plus GST each time that happens. Eligibility depends on the bank's assessment of your profile.

items.title: POP-CLUB fuel waiver capped at Rs 100 a month
items.summary: From 1 June 2026 the 1% fuel surcharge waiver on POP-CLUB only applies to fill-ups between INR 1,000 and INR 3,500, and you can get back at most INR 100 per statement cycle. The card's earlier listed waiver cap was INR 300 per statement cycle.

items.title: ATM cash withdrawals get costlier: min fee now Rs 650
items.summary: Pulling cash out on your credit card will cost at least INR 650 instead of INR 500 (or 2.5% of the amount, whichever is more) from 15 June 2026. Interest also starts from day one on cash withdrawals.

items.title: Elite+ and YES Essence forex markup up to 3%
items.summary: Foreign currency spends on these cards will be charged 3% instead of 2.75%. Small bump, but it applies to every international transaction.

items.title: Failed auto-debit penalty jumps, cap rises to Rs 5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces, you'll pay 2.5% or INR 500 (whichever is higher) instead of 2% or INR 450 from 15 June 2026. The monthly ceiling on these charges also rises from INR 1,500 to INR 5,000 per statement.

items.title: Foreign spends cost more on Reserv and YES First cards
items.summary: Overseas and international online spends on these cards will be marked up 2.00% instead of 1.75% from 15 June 2026. On a INR 50,000 foreign spend that's INR 125 extra plus GST.

items.title: YES Prosperity Business forex markup 2.5% to 3%
items.summary: Overseas and foreign-currency spends on this card now carry a 3% markup instead of 2.5%. That's ₹250 more on a ₹50,000 foreign spend.

items.title: Forex markup 3.4% to 3.5% on Prosperity, POP-CLUB cards
items.summary: International transactions on these cards will be charged 3.5% instead of 3.4%. A small increase applied to every foreign-currency spend.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver now starts at Rs 500 spends
items.summary: From 15 June 2026 the fuel surcharge waiver applies to a new transaction range per card, with most cards needing a minimum fill-up of INR 500 instead of INR 400, and the top of the range dropping to INR 4,000 or INR 3,000 on many cards. Fill-ups outside your card's range get no 1% waiver.

items.title: New ₹250 fee for paying your bill by cheque
items.summary: Paying your card bill by cheque at a YES Bank branch will now cost ₹250 plus GST if the amount is ₹1,000 or more. There was no such fee listed before.

items.title: Select, ACE and Klick forex markup jumps to 3.5%
items.summary: Foreign currency spends on these cards will be charged 3.50% instead of 2.75% from 15 June 2026. That's INR 375 on a INR 50,000 overseas spend, before GST.

items.title: Horizon card free with new Burgundy Savings A/c
items.summary: The ₹3,000 joining and annual fee on the Horizon card is nil if you open a Burgundy Savings Account on or after 1 July 2026. The waiver depends on you keeping that Burgundy relationship.

items.title: Magnus fee waived for new Burgundy Salary users
items.summary: You save the ₹12,500 joining and annual fee on the Magnus card if you open a Burgundy Salary Account on or after 1 July 2026. Everyone else keeps paying ₹12,500.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad now costs 1.5%, not 1%
items.summary: If you let a foreign shop or an overseas-registered website bill you in rupees, Axis now takes 1.5% plus GST of the amount instead of 1%. Burgundy Private, Olympus and Primus cards pay nothing.

items.title: Rent fee no longer capped at Rs 1,500
items.summary: The 1% charge on rent payments has lost its Rs 1,500 per transaction ceiling, so a large rent payment now costs 1% of the whole amount plus GST. Olympus and Primus cards are exempt from the fee.

items.title: Infinia now needs ₹18L spend a year to keep
items.summary: From 1 April 2026, HDFC will only let you keep your Infinia card if you spend ₹18 lakh in a financial year (primary + add-ons) or hold ₹50 lakh in average bank balances. Fall short and the bank can move you to a different card.

items.title: New 1.75% markup on rupee spends abroad
items.summary: From 15 May 2026, paying in rupees at an overseas merchant or an India-based merchant registered abroad will cost you an extra 1.75% of the transaction. This applies even though you never touched foreign currency.

items.title: Late fee on Insta Jumbo loan EMIs from June 2026
items.summary: If you miss or partly pay an Insta Jumbo loan EMI from 20 June 2026, a late fee plus GST kicks in, ranging from ₹100 on small dues to ₹1,300 when you owe over ₹50,000. Nothing is charged if the outstanding is ₹100 or less.

items.title: Government payments now counted as utility spends
items.summary: Government payments are treated as utility transactions, so they earn only the (usually capped) utility reward rate on your card. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: No reward points on rent or wallet top-ups
items.summary: Rent payments and loading money into e-wallets earn you zero reward points, so those spends are effectively unrewarded. Amazon Pay ICICI Bank Credit Card is not affected.

items.title: Free airport lounge needs ₹75,000 spend a quarter
items.summary: Complimentary domestic lounge visits are earned, not given: you must spend ₹75,000 in the previous quarter to get access in the next quarter. Rent, government, education and EMI payments, fees and interest do not count towards that ₹75,000.

items.title: Paying in rupees abroad gets a new fee from 15 Jan 2026
items.summary: From 15 January 2026 ICICI Bank charges a revised Dynamic Currency Conversion fee every time you let an overseas machine (or a foreign-registered merchant in India) bill you in rupees — 3.50% on most cards, 2.00% on Emeralde cards, 1.99% on Amazon Pay, 1.49% on Times Black and 0.99% on the MakeMyTrip Travel card. Always choose to pay in the local currency to avoid it.

items.title: Free movie benefit now needs ₹25,000 spend a quarter
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 your BookMyShow offer is no longer automatic — you must spend ₹25,000 in the previous quarter to unlock it for the next quarter. Spend less and you get no movie benefit that quarter.

items.title: Cardless ATM cash withdrawal being scrapped
items.summary: From 21 February 2026 you can no longer pull cash from RBL or other ATMs using IMT cardless withdrawal, so you'll need your debit card. The Rs. 20 per transaction fee for the service goes away along with the service itself.

items.title: Monthly limit on cashing in reward points
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 you can convert only 60,000 reward points a month into statement credit, so large point balances take longer to use up. Air India SBI Signature and both PhonePe SBI cards are not affected.

items.title: Points redeemed only in blocks of 4,000
items.summary: From 1 April 2026 statement-credit redemptions must be in multiples of 4,000 points, so leftover points below that stay stuck on your account. The two PhonePe SBI cards are excluded from this rule.

items.title: BPCL card: spend 1 lakh to dodge Rs.499 fee
items.summary: From 1 May 2026 you must spend Rs.1 lakh a year on your BPCL SBI Card to get the Rs.499 annual fee refunded, double the earlier Rs.50,000. Spend less and you simply pay the fee.

items.title: Late payment now costs you on small bills too
items.summary: From 1 May 2026, missing a payment on a bill as small as Rs.100 will cost you Rs.100, where earlier anything up to Rs.500 was free. The Rs.500–Rs.1,000 slab also rises from Rs.400 to Rs.500.

items.title: No points on tolls, jewellery, fees on PhonePe cards
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your PhonePe SBI cards stop earning any reward points on tolls, gifts, jewellery, school and college fees, and on utility, insurance or UPI payments made outside the PhonePe app. These everyday spends will now earn you zero.

items.title: PhonePe Select Black: reward caps halved
items.summary: From 1 July 2026 your PhonePe SBI Card SELECT BLACK earns fewer points monthly — PhonePe spends fall from 2,000 points to 1,500 (500 on insurance), and online spends fall from 2,000 to 1,000. Anything above the cap earns you nothing.

items.title: Overspending your limit will cost INR 550
items.summary: YES BANK is bringing back the overlimit facility from 1 June 2026, letting transactions go through above your credit limit — but each one costs INR 550 plus GST. If you would rather not pay this, keep your spending inside your limit.

items.title: POP-Club fuel waiver limited to INR 1,000-3,500 spends
items.summary: From 1 June 2026, POP-Club cardholders only get the 1% fuel surcharge waiver on fills between INR 1,000 and INR 3,500, capped at INR 100 per statement cycle. Fills below INR 1,000 or above INR 3,500 get no waiver.

items.title: Cash withdrawal on your card gets costlier
items.summary: Taking cash out on your YES BANK credit card will cost you at least INR 650 instead of INR 500 from 15 June 2026. The 2.5% rate stays the same, but the minimum floor fee goes up.

items.title: Failed auto-debit fee jumps, cap rises to INR 5,000
items.summary: If your auto-pay bounces, the fee rises from 2% (min INR 450) to 2.5% (min INR 500) from 15 June 2026. Worse, the monthly cap on these charges goes from INR 1,500 to INR 5,000 per statement.

items.title: Forex markup rises on most YES BANK cards
items.summary: Spending abroad or on foreign websites gets more expensive from 15 June 2026 on several cards — for example Reserv and YES First Preferred go from 1.75% to 2%, Elite+ from 2.75% to 3%, and Select/Ace from 2.75% to 3.5%. YES Private, Marquee, FREO and BYOC rates stay unchanged.

items.title: Fuel surcharge waiver window changes on many cards
items.summary: From 15 June 2026 the transaction amounts that qualify for the 1% fuel surcharge waiver change by card — most cards move from INR 400–5,000 to bands like INR 500–5,000, INR 500–4,000 or INR 500–3,000, so small fill-ups under INR 500 no longer qualify. Paisabazaar Paisasave holders move from INR 500–3,000 to INR 500–3,000 range under the new table.

items.title: New INR 250 fee for paying by cheque
items.summary: From 15 June 2026, paying your card bill by cheque at a branch costs INR 250 plus GST if the amount is INR 1,000 or more. There was no such fee before.

items.summary: KredMe helps you pick the best credit card at every purchase. Add your cards to get started.
